events.title: PG&E (PCG) and Edison (EIX) Sink After California Wildfire Liability Deal Falls Apart
events.summary: PG&E (PCG) and Edison (EIX) shares plunged after California lawmakers introduced a bill updating wildfire response that failed to shift liability away from publicly traded utilities, omitting Governor Gavin Newsom's proposal to prevent insurers from suing utilities. This omission led to analyst downgrades and PG&E announcing a strategic review and a $2 billion cut to its 2027 capital investment plan. While future legislative reforms could offer a rebound, unresolved wildfire liabilities are expected to remain a significant challenge for both companies.

articles.headline: PG&E (PCG) and Edison (EIX) Sink After California Wildfire Liability Deal Falls Apart

events.title: ADP employment data and consumer credit among releases due Tuesday

events.title: Tesla Plus SpaceX Could Become a ‘Must-Have’ Investment, Ross Gerber Says
events.summary: Ross Gerber, CEO of Gerber Kawasaki, believes that a merger between Tesla and SpaceX is inevitable and would create a "must-have" investment. He stated that he sees stronger long-term potential in SpaceX than in Tesla due to challenges with Tesla's autonomous driving technology and its focus on Robotaxi. JPMorgan also suggests a merger is strategically coherent and more financially practical now due to SpaceX's higher valuation.

events.title: EVI Industries Completes Acquisition of Sudsies, Inc.
events.summary: EVI Industries has completed its acquisition of Sudsies, Inc., a Miami-based garment care business, establishing its new consumer garment care services division. This acquisition marks EVI's first expansion beyond commercial laundry since 2016, aiming to build a national-scale consumer garment care enterprise while preserving Sudsies' brand and leadership. EVI has grown significantly since 2016, acquiring 32 commercial laundry businesses and increasing its annual revenue to nearly $435 million.

articles.headline: EVI Industries Completes Acquisition of Sudsies, Inc.

events.title: Which Solar Stock Has Dominated in 2026: SolarEdge, Enphase Energy, or First Solar?
events.summary: In 2026, SolarEdge Technologies outperformed its peers, surging 19%, while Enphase Energy rose 13%, and First Solar, despite being the most profitable, dropped 22%. This divergence was driven by policy changes like the expiration of the Section 25D residential clean energy credit, which negatively impacted residential demand and affected Enphase and SolarEdge. SolarEdge's recovery from depressed levels and its commercial/industrial market share contributed to its success, whereas First Solar faced challenges from securities litigation and policy uncertainties.

articles.headline: Which Solar Stock Has Dominated in 2026: SolarEdge, Enphase Energy, or First Solar?
